title: Security model for Agent Studio and the operator agent
summary: Target security model for the move to a public website: threat model per actor, five trust zones, the operator agent as a first-class actor (own identity, scoped short-lived credentials, tiers T0 to T3, recorded standing grants, owner approval with step-up, hash-chained audit with an off-host sink, break-glass, kill switch, rules for untrusted content and several sessions), agent containment, credential placement with a takeover runbook, a public deployment baseline and four stages. Alternatives compare five operator credential models, four host separation options and three audit stores. Recommended: typed operations with short-lived certificates as transition, hash-chained audit with a write-once sink, separate users and per-attempt containers now and a separate control-plane host before a second user. Thirteen slices ordered by stage; the first gives the operator agent its own identity and audit trail.

implementationTasks.title: SM-1 · Operator agent identity and audit trail
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Operator agent identity and audit trail

Source: docs/security-model/index.html (AGT-3353), decisions SM-D1, SM-D4, SM-D11. Read that Dossier and workbench.json first, then AGENTS.md, docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html and docs/operations/security/overview.md. Use the Dossier's recommended option for each named decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented.

Stage: 0 · owner only behind an access layer. Dependencies: none (first slice). Resolve slice IDs to promoted task keys before starting dependent work.

Entry points: backend/Features/Security/Iam/ (service accounts, AccessSecurityStore.Iam.cs), backend/Features/Security/ (middleware and audit writers), TaskServerPrincipalStore in task-server/, card timeline actors.

## Deliver
Add a principal kind `operator-agent` built on the service-account model, with child sessions. The Owner creates the operator principal and starts a session in Settings > Access; each session receives its own bearer token (at most 8 hours, renewable only by the Owner). Every request, audit entry and card timeline event made with a session token carries the actor `operator-agent:<id>/session:<sid>` and `delegatedBy: human:<owner id>`; the owner never appears as the actor. Introduce one audit writer for the control plane: entries carry actor, session, route or operation, target, parameter digest, outcome, time and the hash of the previous entry; route the existing IAM, service-account, API-token, secret and run audits through it without dropping fields. Forward each entry to a configurable off-host append-only sink (start with an HTTPS endpoint or object storage with write-once retention behind an adapter) and record the forwarded position. Add a verification job that recomputes the chain and compares it with the sink, raising an acute alert on a gap or mismatch. Add an operator activity view for the Owner that lists sessions and their entries. Document how the operator agent is configured on the owner's machine under its own OS user, without access to the owner's SSH agent or keys (D11).

## Out of scope
Tiers, grants and approvals (SM-4, SM-5); host certificates (SM-6); the kill switch beyond revoking a single token (SM-2).

## Acceptance
- In a scripted operator session of at least 50 mixed requests, 100% of audit entries and timeline events name the operator agent and session, and 0 name the owner.
- Changing, deleting or reordering any stored audit entry makes the verification job fail and raise an alert in a test.
- Entries reach the configured sink within 60 seconds at the 95th percentile in a test with a fake sink; an unreachable sink queues entries without loss and alerts.
- An operator session token cannot call access administration, write audit or create grants (403 in tests).

Verification and documentation
Reproduce the gap with a failing test before the fix. Build any credential-shaped test value at runtime; never write provider-shaped literals. Do not include real hostnames, addresses or account names in code, tests, docs or commits; the repository is public. UI changes follow frontend/AGENTS.md and docs/quality/design/style-guide-hard-rules.md and need Playwright coverage with light and dark screenshots under results/. Update docs/operations/security/overview.md and the affected setup guide, append to this Dossier's implementation log, and report exact verification. Git handling stays with the platform: do not commit, push or manage worktrees yourself.

# Kill switch and operator sessions

Source: docs/security-model/index.html (AGT-3353), decisions SM-D1, SM-D7. Entry points: Settings > Access, the operator principal from SM-1, Operations Server principal revocation (operations-server/Features/Access/), backend session middleware.

## Deliver
Add an Owner action `End all operator access` in Studio and an equivalent out-of-band command on the control-plane host for when the UI is unreachable. Add a scheduled drill mode that exercises the switch against a test principal and records the measured time.

Grant model and approval UI.

# Operation catalogue, tiers and standing grants

Source: docs/security-model/index.html (AGT-3353), decisions SM-D2, SM-D3, SM-D7. ## Deliver
Define an operation catalogue for the operator agent: each catalogued route or typed operation has an id, a tier (T0 observe, T1 routine, T2 high risk) and a scope kind.
